neighbours.label: The word 'population' in a count of the people of a place (a weak guess; the pole's top examples are otherwise unexplained)
fire: By 1850 the mill town had a Welsh population of about 2,000 in a total of 7,500.
Official figures show a steep fall in the population after the famine.
Fewer than sixty Quakers lived in the borough's population of 4,200.
Historians estimate that the plague halved the population of the port.
Parish books record a marked rise in the population during those years.
Only 300 Greeks remained in the island's population by the end of the war.
The governor worried about a shrinking population across the northern districts.
Before the dam was built, the valley's population was about 900.
quiet: By 1850 the mill town had a Welsh choir of about 20 in a hall for 750.
Official figures show a steep fall in the wages after the famine.
Fewer than sixty Quakers lived in the borough's streets near the mill.
Historians estimate that the plague halved the income of the port.
Parish books record a marked rise in the rents during those years.
Only 300 Greeks remained on the island by the end of the war.
The governor worried about a shrinking budget across the northern districts.
Before the dam was built, the valley's river was about 90 feet wide.

notes: Top examples are mixed (division, people, is, skin, reboot); ' population' is the only repeat. If this holds, coverage should show it explains little of the pole.
